top_choice_rationale: Pd-catalysed C-N cross-coupling is the most mature and best-verified achievement on the slate: ligand design made aryl amination general and predictable, the mechanism is established, adoption in pharmaceutical and materials synthesis is checkable, and the allocation to Buchwald and Hartwig is clean, with Kosugi a precursor. A citation naming carbon-nitrogen coupling separates it from the 2010 C-C coupling prize. P001 is a strong second: a genuinely new induced-proximity principle with a sound mechanism, but part of the chemistry is ligand and linker optimisation on known E3 binders, no PROTAC is yet approved, and the three-name cut omits decisive contributors. Either is preferable to no award.
